{{Quote|No job is over this little guy's head.|R2-series advertising slogan|<ref name="NEGTD" />}}
The '''R2-series astromech droid''' was a model of [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]] produced by [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|Industrial Automaton]], boasting a level of success that was never equaled in Industrial Automaton's long history. A combination of excellent design, high-quality marketing, and good timing made this astromech droid one of the most sought after [[Droid/Legends|droids]] in [[Timeline of galactic history/Legends|history]], and one of the few vintage astromech series still in active production decades after it was first designed, including the prototype [[R2-0]]. The line was so successful, even being given a positive review by ''[[Mechtech Illustrated/Legends|Mechtech Illustrated]]'' for its versatility, that the [[Galactic Empire/Legends|Galactic Empire]] would later take credit for the design. The average cost for an R2 unit was about 4245 Republic Credits.

==Description==
The R2-series [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech]] was a barrel-shaped [[Droid/Legends|droid]]<ref name="J7" /> that stood 0.96 [[Meter/Legends|meters]] tall.<ref name="NEGTD" /> The droids were designed to be adaptable, with modular software components and they were easy to upgrade with other hardware to fit an owner's specific needs. Industrial Automaton manufactured a number of additional appendages, tools, and equipment that could be installed on an R2 unit, as did a number of other third-party corporations.<ref name="J7" /> R2s had a streamlined design,<ref name="EGTD">''[[The Essential Guide to Droids]]''</ref> with all of the appendages and equipment tucked away and hidden behind panels.<ref name="J7" /> A fully rotatable domed head sat on the torso, and locomotion was provided by three [[Tread/Legends|motorized treaded]] legs, with the middle leg capable of retracting into the droid's body.<ref name="EGTD" /> The R2 was available in a variety of [[Color/Legends|colors]], with special designer iridescents that were exclusive to the inhabitants of the [[Core Worlds/Legends|Core Worlds]].<ref name="J7" />

R2 units were equipped with an [[Intellex IV/Legends|Intellex IV]] [[Computer/Legends|computer]] which stored over seven hundred different [[Starship/Legends|spacecraft]] configurations in a comprehensive [[ROM]] library. The internal computer was used by the droid to perform duties such as monitoring and analyzing flight performance, scanning technical files to diagnose problems, examine data patterns, and debug computer coding. The Intellex IV could process over 10,000 MPF operations every [[Standard second|second]]. R2s could store up to ten sets of [[Hyperspace/Legends|hyperspace]] coordinates in its [[RAM|active memory]], allowing them to assist spacecraft with limited [[Navigation computer/Legends|navigation computer]] capabilities to perform hyperspace jumps.<ref name="RPG">[[Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game (first edition)|''Star Wars: The Roleplaying Game'']]</ref>

[[File:R2socket.jpg|thumb|right|175px|R2 units could interface directly with [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] through large sockets, such as on an [[Eta-2 Actis-class interceptor/Legends|Eta-2]].]]
R2 units were fully rated to operate flawlessly in the [[Vacuum/Legends|vacuum]] of [[Realspace/Legends|space]],<ref name="EGTD" /> and they were designed to perform as a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]] interface droid. This was considered a bold move on Industrial Automaton's part, as such configurations were usually reserved for military droids, and the R2 was marketed as a commercial model. Industrial Automaton used their impressive legal connections to have the regulations surrounding the issue changed to allow the R2 to function in its intended capacity.<ref name="J7" /> When plugged into the [[Astromech socket/Legends|astromech socket]] of a [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighter]], the R2 monitored the craft's flight performance, solved technical issues, and boosted power to the onboard systems. The droid was also capable of performing tasks such as [[Engine/Legends|engine]] startup and pre-flight taxiing.<ref name="EGTD" /> 

Standard equipment for the R2 included two all-purpose [[Manipulator arm/Legends|manipulator arms]] with a reach of .85 meters. One was a [[Grasper arm/Legends|heavy-duty grasper]] with a lifting capacity of twenty-five [[Kilogram/Legends|kilograms]] and a grasping pressure of ten kilograms. The other was a fine manipulator with only a two kilogram lifting capacity, but it had exceptional maneuverability with three 360-degree rotational joints and precise micro-adjustment controls that gave the arm  a better than one [[micrometer]] placement accuracy.<ref name="RPG" /> Other equipment included an electric [[Arc welder/Legends|arc welder]], [[Circular saw/Legends|circular saw]], a [[Holoprojector/Legends|holoprojector]]<ref name="EGTD" /> with [[MultiPhase sound]],<ref name="RPG" /> [[Fire extinguisher/Legends|fire extinguisher]],<ref name="EGTD" /> [[Laser cutter/Legends|laser cutter]], high-powered [[Spotlight/Legends|spotlights]],<ref name="RPG" /> and an internal cargo compartment.<ref name="EGTD" /> A retractable [[I/O jack]] allowed the R2 to create a direct hardwired connection with standard computer ports<ref name="RPG" /> and they were equipped with a [[Holographic recording mode/Legends|holographic recording mode]].<ref name="Star Wars radio">[[Star Wars (radio)|''Star Wars'' radio drama]]</ref>

[[File:R2D2-SWIACD.png|thumb|left|180px|The many modifications of [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]].]]
The droid's [[Sensor/Legends|sensor]] package incorporated a [[Full-spectrum transceiver/Legends|full-spectrum transceiver]],<ref name="EGTD" /> [[electro photo receptor]]s, and [[Dedicated energy receptor/Legends|dedicated energy receptors]],<ref name="RPG" /> along with [[Electromagnetic sensor|electromagnetic]], [[Heat detector|heat]], [[Motion sensor/Legends|motion]], and [[Life-form scanner/Legends|life-form detectors]].<ref name="EGTD" /> All of the sensors were routed through the R2's [[Intellex IV/Legends|Intellex IV]] which supported sophisticated analysis programs.<ref name="RPG" /> The R2 unit was equipped with an extendible and fully maneuverable [[video sensor]] that could be used to inspect small, enclosed spaces.<ref name="EGTD" /> The sensor had a maximum reach of 0.85 meters, and featured a full 360-degree rotational joint.<ref name="RPG" />

R2 units had built-in telecom software that allowed it to communicate with computers under the jurisdiction of both the [[Imperial Navy Transmission]] and the [[Corporate Sector Standard]] communications systems, as well as being given custom communications software.<ref name="RPG" /> Industrial Automaton ensured that the droid was easy to modify and upgrade. Modified R2s have included equipment as diverse as [[underwater propeller]]s, [[laser pointer]]s, [[zero-gee maneuvering jet]]s, [[remote sensor limpet]]s, and [[inflatable life raft]]s.<ref name="EGTD" />

Various models of the R2-series were produced, one of which being the [[Model D R2-series astromech droid|D model]]. The Ds were renowned as good models that were extremely versatile and particularly adept at astromechanical and stellar navigation. While well rounded, they also had a reputation for being a little erratic.<ref name="PoT>''[[Planet of Twilight]]''</ref>  

==Role==
[[File:R2_schematic.jpg|thumb|right|180px|Technical schematics of an R2 unit from one of [[Industrial Automaton/Legends|IA's]] [[HoloNet/Legends|HoloNet]] advertisements.]]

Similar to its predecessors, the [[P2-series astromech droid|P2-series]] and [[R1-series astromech droid/Legends|R1-series]], the R2 was designed to operate on [[Starship/Legends|starships]] as a diagnostic and repair [[Technician/Legends|technician]]. Unlike the larger models, the R2's waist-high height allowed it to interface with military [[Starfighter/Legends|starfighters]] as well.<ref name="EGTD" />

Due to the enhanced [[Personality matrix/Legends|personality matrix]] installed in the droid,<ref name="J7" /> R2 units developed personalities that were considered to be obliging, quick-witted, and sincere.<ref name="EGTD" /> They had the tendency to develop pleasant and distinctive personalities<ref name="J7" /> with a headstrong self-reliant streak if [[Memory wipe/Legends|memory wipes]] were not performed on a regular basis. However, owners often found that they preferred the droid to have a personality and a willingness to offer candid second opinions.<ref name="EGTD" />

==History==
The R2-series of astromech droid was created as a follow-up to Industrial Automaton's successful and highly regarded R1-series.<ref name="RPG" /> Industrial Automaton monitored consumer trends and discovered that the sale of small starships had risen, taking up nearly forty percent of the overall market. Conversely, the trend in droids was for larger models such as Industrial Automaton's own R1, [[Zubintech]]'s [[T-831]], and [[Delban Faxicorp]]'s [[DBX]]. Industrial Automaton thought small, and designed a droid that was intended to take advantage of the fact that there were more personal starships in [[The galaxy/Legends|the galaxy]] than ever before.<ref name="J7" />

Upon its release, the R2 was an instant success and dominated the small-droid market.<ref name="EGTD" /> A positive review from ''[[Mechtech Illustrated/Legends|Mechtech Illustrated]]'' stated that the R2 was "one of the most versatile, multitalented droids we've ever seen. The R2 unit can do it all."<ref name="EGTD" /> At least by the time of the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]], R2 purchases came with a three-year warranty, a user-support hotline, IA quality, various affordable prices, and dealer financing.<ref name="RPG" />

Due to its ability to be used in the [[Astromech socket/Legends|astromech sockets]] of starfighters, R2 units became popular with [[Galactic Republic/Legends|Galactic Republic]] fighter [[Pilot/Legends|pilots]].<ref name="EGTD" /> Following the Galactic Civil War, sales of the R2-series increased due to the fact one of the units, [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], was one of the most famous figures of the conflict. Industrial Automaton did not use R2's accomplishments in their advertising, mainly to maintain a strong relationship with the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]] government, but they continued to produce the R2-series.<ref name="EGTD" />

==Notable units==
===R2-D2===
{{Main| R2-D2/Legends}}
{{Quote|An extremely well-put-together little droid, Your Highness. Without a doubt, it saved the ship, as well as our lives.|[[Captain/Legends|Captain]] [[Quarsh Panaka/Legends|Quarsh Panaka]] to [[Queen/Legends|Queen]] [[Padmé Amidala/Legends|Amidala]]|<ref name="Episode 1" />}}
The most notable R2-series astromech droid was R2-D2. He participated in numerous battles during both the [[Clone Wars/Legends|Clone Wars]] and the [[Galactic Civil War/Legends|Galactic Civil War]]. It was R2 who helped deliver the [[Death Star plans/Legends|Death Star plans]] to the Rebellion, allowing their victory at the [[Battle of Yavin/Legends|Battle of Yavin]], and a message from [[Princess/Legends|Princess]] [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia]] to [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi]], which caused [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] to leave [[Tatooine/Legends|Tatooine]] and go on to become a [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]].<ref name="ANH">{{Film|IV}}</ref>
